docs.text: The steps below start from an empty project and end with a sheet. Every step names what to click in the BIMopen interface style, the one BIMopen starts in; the interface chapter explains each part of the window.

docs.title: 1. Start a new project
docs.text:
1. Click BIMopen's mark at the top of the rail: the application menu opens.
  2. Click New ▸ Project…. The New project dialog proposes BIMopen's default template: click OK.
Step 1: the application menu

The new project has two levels, Ground Floor and First Floor, a floor plan for each, and the default 3D view. It has no walls yet. Its wall, door, window, floor and roof types are ready to use.

docs.title: 2. Open the ground floor plan
docs.text:
In the views strip under the drawing area, click the thumbnail Floor Plan: Ground Floor. The plan opens in the drawing area, and the top bar and the view selector show Floor Plan: Ground Floor.

Note

Views on the rail also shows the Project Index, the tree of every view: there, a single click on a view shows its properties in the element panel without opening it, and a double-click opens it.

docs.title: 3. Draw four walls
docs.text:
1. In the tools of Create, the rail entry BIMopen opens with, click Wall in the Build group (if the tool panel is folded, click Create on the rail first). The contextual card Draw Wall comes on top of the tool panel, the options strip over the view shows the settings of the wall, and the element panel shows the type of the next wall, Exterior wall - Clay block 300 + ETICS.
  2. In the status bar, turn on Ortho: the walls stay horizontal or vertical.
  3. Click in the plan where the first corner goes. The status bar asks for the next point: WALL next point [Esc to finish]:.
  1. Click the second, third and fourth corners. While you move the mouse, the length and the angle of the wall being drawn are shown next to it.
  2. Click the first corner again: the four walls are joined at the corners.
  3. Press Esc to stop the chain, and Esc again to end the tool.

Tip

You can draw the same walls by typing their corners in metres: wall 0,0 10,0 10,6 0,6 c. The final c closes the chain. See Command line and MCP.

docs.title: 4. Add a door and a window
docs.text:
1. Click Create ▸ Build ▸ Door, then click on a wall where the door goes. The door is placed in the wall, which is cut around it. The command log confirms it: Door «Single swing door 80x210» in wall ….
  2. Press Esc: the tool ends and the contextual card goes away.
  3. Click Create ▸ Build ▸ Window, click on another wall, and press Esc.

A door or a window can only be placed in a wall: after a click away from the walls, the command line answers no wall at that point and nothing is placed.

docs.title: 5. Add a floor and a roof
docs.text:
1. Click Create ▸ Build ▸ Flooring. Sketch mode opens: the contextual card Edit | Create Floor Boundary, with Pick Walls active.
  2. Move the cursor over a wall and press Tab: the four walls are highlighted. Click: their lines go on the inner faces of the walls.
  3. Click Finish Edit Mode: the floor is made and the command log gives its area.
  4. Click Create ▸ Build ▸ Roof. Pick Walls is active again; the options strip has Defines Slope (ticked) and the Overhang (500 mm by default).
  5. Press Tab over a wall, click, then Finish Edit Mode: a hip roof sloping at 30° covers the walls, with the overhang all around.
Step 5: walls, door, window, floor and roof

Floors, roofs, stairs and components tells more about sketch mode.

docs.title: 6. Look at it in 3D
docs.text:
Click the {3D} thumbnail in the views strip. The default 3D view, {3D}, opens. Drag with the right mouse button (or with Shift and the middle button) to orbit, drag with the middle button to pan, and turn the wheel to zoom; the left button selects, as in plans. Home fits the whole model in the view.

Step 6: the house in 3D

docs.title: 7. Put the plan on a sheet
docs.text:
1. Click Document on the rail, then Sheet in the Sheets group. The New Sheet dialog lists the title blocks: none, A0, A1, A2 or A3, with their size in millimetres.
  2. Click OK. The sheet is created with the next free number (A101 for the first one, then A102…) and opens.
  3. Click Document ▸ Sheets ▸ View. The Views dialog lists the views that are not on a sheet yet.
  4. Choose Floor Plan: Ground Floor and click Add View to Sheet. A rectangle of the plan's size follows the cursor: click on the sheet where the plan goes. It is placed at its own scale, 1 : 100, as a viewport, which stays selected.
Step 7: the plan on a sheet

docs.title: 8. Undo, redo and save
docs.text:
• Ctrl+Z undoes the last change (here, the viewport goes away); Ctrl+Y redoes it. The arrows of the top bar, Undo and Redo, do the same.
  • Ctrl+S saves the project, as a click on the save state in the top bar. A project that has never been saved asks for a file name first; the file has the extension .bimopen. In the browser, the file is downloaded.

The top bar says Unsaved changes while there are changes to save, and Saved after saving.

docs.title: What next
docs.text:
• The interface describes every part of the window.
  • Keyboard shortcuts lists the keys and the two-letter shortcuts, such as WA for a wall.
  • Command line and MCP shows how to type commands, run scripts and let an agent model for you.

docs.title: Interface styles
docs.text:
BIMopen has two interface styles and a touch mode. All of them run the same commands, with the same names, keyboard shortcuts and results; only the look and the place of the tools change.

  • The BIMopen style, described in The interface and pictured throughout this manual: the rail, the tool panel, the command search, the element panel and the strip of views. BIMopen starts in this style.
  • The Classic style: the ribbon with its tabs, the options bar, the Properties palette and the Project Index in panels.
  • Touch mode: the layout for touch screens and pens, on a touch monitor, a tablet or a phone.

docs.title: Choosing the style
docs.text:
1. Click the gear at the right end of the top bar, or open the application menu and choose Options.
  2. Under User Interface, set Interface to Classic or BIMopen. BIMopen starts in the BIMopen style.

The window changes at once. The choice is remembered, on the desktop and in the browser, and the next session starts in the same style. Theme (Light or Dark) applies to both styles.

The BIMopen style in the dark theme

In Arabic the whole window is mirrored, in every style: the rail and the tool panel, or the palettes, are on the right, the element panel on the left.

docs.title: The Classic style
docs.text:
The Classic style Part Where What it holds Title bar Top The quick access toolbar (Open…, Save, Undo, Redo and the tools you add), the project and the active view, the light or dark theme and the ? menu Ribbon Under the title bar File, which opens the application menu, then the tabs (Model, Structure, Reinforced concrete, Metal, Prefabrication, MEP, Link and import, Annotations, Check, Massing & site, Collaborate, Views, Project) with their groups of buttons, and the contextual tab while a tool works or something is selected Options bar Under the ribbon The options of the active tool, as the options strip of the BIMopen style, and at its right end what the tool expects or the element under the cursor, the selection count and Select and Drag; right-click it for Dock at Bottom Properties and Project Index Left The element panel's Properties tab, and the Project Index of Views, as panels that dock on either side or float Drawing area Centre The views, each with its view control bar at the bottom (scale, detail, crop, isolate) and the navigation bar on its right edge (Zoom to Fit, Zoom In, Zoom Out, Zoom Options) Command line Under the drawing area The log and the prompt; what you type in a view goes there Views and families strip Bottom The same strip as in the BIMopen style

The rail entries of the BIMopen style hold the ribbon's tabs: Create the tabs from Model to Massing & site, Document the sheets of Views and Annotations, Views the rest of Views and the Project Index, Coordinate Check and Collaborate, Settings Project.

docs.title: Everything of the Classic style
docs.text:
Every function of the Classic style is in the BIMopen style, once:

  • every button of the ribbon is a tile of the tool panel, in the rail entry that holds its tab, and the contextual Modify tab is the card on top of the panel while a tool works or something is selected;
  • BIMopen's mark at the top of the rail opens the application menu; the top bar has undo, redo, the quick access tools and the ? menu;
  • Views holds the whole Project Index, with its menus;
  • a thumbnail of the view strip can be dragged onto the open sheet, or onto a sheet's thumbnail, and its right-click menu has the browser's actions and Open in the active window;
  • the view selector's menu arranges the view windows (Switch View, Tile, Cascade, Maximize, Replicate, Close Hidden); Ctrl+Tab goes to the previous window;
  • the right button on a tile offers Add to Quick Access Toolbar: the tool shows in the top bar, works from any section of the rail, and its right button offers Remove from Quick Access Toolbar;
  • the key tips work as on the ribbon: tap Alt (or press F10), then a tab's letter opens the rail section that holds it (its letter shows on the rail) and a tool's letters start it.

docs.title: Touch mode
docs.text: Touch mode lays the interface out for touch screens and pens: phones, tablets and touch monitors. It runs the same commands as the two styles, with the same names; only the layout changes, and every control is big enough for a finger.

docs.title: Turning it on
docs.text:
Options ▸ User Interface ▸ Touch mode has three values:

Value Effect Automatic On where the device is touch first: in a browser with a finger as pointer or a window at most 900 pixels wide, and on Android. On the desktop it stays off Always Always on, on the desktop too (a touch monitor, a tablet PC) Never Never on

BIMopen remembers the choice with the other preferences. Menu ▸ Leave touch mode brings back the other interface until the next start.

docs.title: Phone, landscape and tablet
docs.text:
The layout follows the room the window has.

On a touch monitor, or any wide window (here 1920 × 1080): the rail on the left opens a palette of tools for each category (Model, Structure, MEP, Annotations, Views, Project), the properties stay on the right, the views and families strip at the bottom, and the Command or search field in the top bar, beside Undo, Redo and Pen.

Touch mode on a touch monitor, 1920 × 1080

On a tablet, upright (800 × 1280) or sideways (1280 × 800): the same layout as on a monitor. Where the window is narrow the properties are put away, to leave the room to the drawing: Properties in the top bar brings them back.

Touch mode on a tablet held upright, 800 × 1280 Touch mode on a tablet held sideways, 1280 × 800

On a phone, upright (narrow and tall): a compact top bar with the menu, the project and the view (a tap opens the views), Undo, Redo, Command or search and Pen; the drawing takes the whole width; five big buttons at the bottom, Views, Families, Tools (Modify while something is selected), Properties and Commands, each opening a sheet from the bottom. Drag the sheet's handle up to make it taller, down to make it smaller or close it; a tap outside closes it.

Touch mode on a phone held upright, 412 × 915

On a phone sideways (short and wide): a rail on the left with the categories Model, Structure, MEP, Annotations, Views and Project, plus the views and the properties; the sheets open on the right.

Touch mode on a phone held sideways, 915 × 412

The tools are large tiles with an icon and a name. A tool still to come is greyed, Not available yet; a tool that does not work in the 3D view (Level, Grid, Reference Plane, the annotations) is greyed there, Not available in the 3D view. A tap on a greyed tile says why.

While a tool works, a green strip under the top bar shows its options and Done, which ends it (or finishes a sketch). While you draw a wall, Length… opens the command line: type the length of the next wall and, if needed, its angle, as 4.5 or 4.5 90.

A tap selects, and the selected walls show big grips at their ends. Over the drawing a floating bar offers Move, Copy, Rotate, Mirror, Properties and Delete; a long press opens the context menu. At the bottom left the view button shows the scale and the graphic style and opens Scale, Detail, Graphic style, Sun and shadows, Crop and Isolate Temporarily; at the bottom right Zoom to Fit.

docs.title: Gestures and the pen
docs.text:
Gesture What it does tap selects, or places the point of the active tool drag with one finger as a mouse drag: a selection window, a grip, an element long press the context menu two fingers pan; pinch to zoom; in the 3D view twist to turn the model double tap fits the view in the window

Pen in the top bar is for a pen: the pen draws and selects, fingers only move the view (one finger pans, two fingers pan, zoom and turn). A pen palette on the side of the drawing has Select, Wall, Door, Window, Detail line, Aligned, Text and More tools…. In a browser a pen is told from a finger by the browser; in the desktop app a touch that reports a pressure is taken for a pen.

docs.title: The interface
docs.text:
This chapter describes the BIMopen interface style, the one BIMopen starts in, on the desktop and in the browser. The other looks, the Classic style and touch mode for tablets and phones, run the same commands with the same names; Interface styles shows them and tells how to switch.

The BIMopen window with a wall selected in the ground floor plan

The window has these parts:

  1. the rail, on the left edge: BIMopen's mark, which opens the application menu, then Home, Create, Document, Views and Coordinate, and at the bottom the open project and Settings;
  2. the tool panel, beside the rail: the tools of the rail entry chosen, as cards of tiles;
  3. the top bar: the project and the active view, the command search, which is also the command line, the save state, Undo and Redo, the quick access tools, the light or dark theme, the ? menu and Options;
  4. the drawing area, in the middle: the views, each with its view selector at the top and the view bar at the bottom; while a tool works, the options strip runs over it;
  5. the element panel, on the right: the properties of the selection, or of the active view;
  6. the views and families strip, under the drawing area;
  7. the status bar, along the bottom.

The panels keep their width whatever they show: a long name is cut with «…» and its tooltip shows it whole. Drag the edge of the tool panel or of the element panel to make it wider or narrower; BIMopen remembers it for the next session. A click on the rail entry already chosen folds the tool panel, and a second click opens it again.

In Arabic the whole window is mirrored: the rail and the tool panel are on the right, the element panel on the left, and the strips read from right to left.

docs.title: Application menu
docs.text:
BIMopen's mark, at the top of the rail, opens the application menu: the commands that work on the whole project. The Home entry of the rail shows the project with its levels, views, sheets and schedules, and reminds you that the file commands are in this menu.

Item What it does New Closes the current project and starts a new one from the default template: two levels with their plans, and the default types Open… Opens a .bimopen project, or imports an .rvt file (experimental: only the project name and the level names), chosen in a file dialog. In the browser, drag the file into the page instead Sample project Opens the sample house Save Ctrl+S Saves the project in its file; a project never saved asks for a name, like Save As… Save As… Saves the project in a new .bimopen file and goes on working on that file Print… Ctrl+P Prints sheets to PDF Export ▸ Export IFC4… Writes the model as an IFC4 file Export ▸ Export plan SVG… Writes the active plan as an SVG drawing Export ▸ Export view PNG… Writes the active view as a PNG image Open Documents Lists the open view windows; click one to bring it to the front Options Opens the Options dialog Exit Closes BIMopen (desktop only) The application menu and its Export submenu

New, Open… and Sample project replace the current project without asking: save it first if you want to keep it.

Warning

Unsaved changes are lost when you choose New, Open… or Sample project. The top bar says Unsaved changes while there are changes to save.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
The gear at the right end of the top bar, or Application menu ▸ Options, opens Options. It has, among others, these settings:

Setting Values Effect User Interface ▸ Language Italiano, English, Deutsch, Français, Español, العربية The language of the whole interface, at once User Interface ▸ Theme Light, Dark The colours of the window. Dark also turns on Invert background color. The sun or moon in the top bar switches it too User Interface ▸ Interface BIMopen, Classic The interface style, see Interface styles User Interface ▸ Touch mode Automatic, Always, Never The layout for touch screens, see Interface styles Graphics ▸ Invert background color on, off Views with a dark background and light lines Orientation cube ▸ Orientation cube size, Inactive opacity Small, Medium, Large; 0 % to 100 % The size of the cube, and how much it shows while the pointer is elsewhere Orientation cube ▸ Keep scene upright on, off Dragging the cube never turns the model upside down; off, the view can pass over the top Orientation cube ▸ Fit to view on, off A click on the cube also fits the model in the window Options, Orientation cube tab

docs.title: Top bar and quick access tools
docs.text:
The top bar shows, from the left, BIMopen, the name of the project (a click opens Project information) and the active view; in the middle the command search; on the right:

The top bar Control What it does Saved / Unsaved changes The save state; a click saves, Ctrl+S Undo Undoes the last change, Ctrl+Z. Greyed when there is nothing to undo Redo Redoes the change just undone, Ctrl+Y. Greyed when there is nothing to redo The quick access tools The tools you added, then the arrow of the quick access toolbar The sun or the moon Switches to the light or to the dark theme ? Help F1, Commands (every command of the command line, as typing help) and About (the version, the licence and the credits) The gear Options

Right-click a tile of the tool panel and choose Add to Quick Access Toolbar: the tool shows in the top bar and starts from there whatever rail entry is open. Right-click it there for Remove from Quick Access Toolbar or Add Separator (a line to its right). The small arrow after the tools, Customize Quick Access Toolbar, lists the default tools (Open…, Save, Aligned dimension, Tag by Category, Text, 3D View, Section, Close Hidden, Switch View): tick one to show it, untick it to remove it. In the same menu, Customize Quick Access Toolbar… opens a window with the tools in order: Move Up and Move Down move the one selected, Add Separator puts a line after it, Remove takes it (or a line) away, OK applies. The tools are kept for the next sessions.

Customize Quick Access Toolbar

? ▸ Help (F1) opens this manual, in the language of the interface, in the browser. F1 opens the page of what you are doing: the open dialog, the tile under the mouse (its tip ends with Press F1 for more information) or the active tool.

docs.title: The Create tools
docs.text:
The tools you use most to model are in Create ▸ Modelling ▸ Architecture:

Group Tiles Build Wall WA, Door DR, Window WN, Roof RF, Flooring SB, Object CM, Curtain Grid CG, Mullion MU Vertical Links Railing RA, Stair ST Rooms and Areas Room RM, Room Separator RS, Area ▾ (Area Plan, Area Outline, Area), Legend LG, Settings ▾ (Area and Volume Computations, Color Schemes) References Level: drawn in an elevation or a section, two clicks at the new level's height (from a plan it opens an elevation); Grid GR

Area Outline and Area work in an area plan: until one is open they are greyed, and their tip says to open an area plan first.

docs.text:
Group Tiles Sheets Sheet: a new sheet with the title block you choose; View: places a view on the open sheet Dimension Aligned DI, Linear DL, Angular DA Text Text TX Detail Detail line, Filled region, Masking region, Detail component CD, Repeating detail RD, Insulation IS Tag Tag All TG

Sheets ▸ View works only while a sheet is open.

The Document tools

docs.title: The Views tools
docs.text:
Views on the rail: the tools of the views and the Project Index Group Tiles Create 3D View ▾ (Default 3D View, Save View), Plan ▾ (Floor Plan, Area Plan), Duplicate View ▾ (Duplicate, Duplicate with Detailing), Section SE, Elevation ▾ (Elevation EL, Framing Elevation), Enlarged detail DT (a callout), Free 2D View VD, Schedules ▾ (Schedule/Quantities, Material Takeoff, Sheet List, Note Block, Predefined schedules) Graphics Visibility and Graphics VG, Filters, View templates, Apply template to current view, Create template from current view Windows Switch View, Replicate, Cascade, Tile, Maximize, Close others, Panels

Save View works only while a 3D view is open, and Duplicate with Detailing only for views that are not 3D. Under the tools, the Project Index card holds the whole tree of the project.

Every ▾ menu also lists, greyed, the entries not available yet; the command search finds them all.

docs.title: The Settings tools
docs.text:
Group Tiles Settings Materials, Project information, Styles by Category, Line styles, Purge unused, Project units UN, Snap, and Additional settings (Line styles, Fill patterns) Inquiry Check: checks the openings and references of the model and reports at the command line

Snap turns snapping on and off for the whole program: it is highlighted while on, as the Snap switch of the status bar. Additional settings ▸ Snaps… opens the Snap window: the length and angular increments, the object snaps and the overrides (see Snap).

The Settings tools

docs.title: The contextual card
docs.text:
The wall tool at work: the contextual card on top of the tool panel and the options strip over the view

When you start a tool or select something, a card comes on top of the tool panel, whatever rail entry is open, with the name of what you are doing in the accent colour: Draw Wall while drawing walls, Selection: Walls with walls selected, Multi-Select with elements of different categories, Edit | … in the other modes. When the tool ends, or the selection is cleared, the card goes away; Esc or a click on empty space does the same.

It always has these groups:

Group Tiles Properties Properties: shows or hides the element panel; Type Parameters: the properties of the type of the selection, or of the next element the tool will place Modify Align AL, Offset OF, Mirror on Axis MM, Mirror on Line DM, Split Element SL, Split with Joint SG, Move MV, Copy CO, Rotate RO, Shorten/Lengthen TR, Shorten/Lengthen one element, Shorten/Lengthen several elements, Repeat in Series AR, Scale RE, Fix PN, Unpin UP, Delete (Del)

Delete works only when something is selected. The selecting and modifying chapter describes the Modify tools.

Other groups appear for what is selected or for the tool:

When Group and tiles Anything selected Selection: Filter (see Selecting and modifying) Doors or windows selected Opening: Flip facing, Flip hand Walls selected Modify Wall: Link Top/Base (the walls rise to the roof above them), Unlink Top/Base A level selected View: Open plan Sections or elevations selected Section: Split Segment (sections only), Flip, Go to View A callout selected Detail: Go to View Curtain walls selected Curtain Wall: Curtain Grid, Mullion, Panel Flooring or Roof tool Draw: Boundary Line, Pick Walls Stair or Railing tool Mode: Finish Edit Mode; Draw: Run or Lines Mullion tool Placement: Grid Line, Grid Line Segment, All Grid Lines A detail tool The drawing shapes of the tool The contextual card of a selection

docs.title: Options strip
docs.text:
While a tool works, a strip runs over the top of the view: the name of what you are doing, then the settings of the tool. They apply to the next elements you place.

The options strip Tool Settings on the options strip Wall Height or Depth; the level the wall reaches, or Unconnected with its value; Alignment; Continue; Offset; Radius (greyed: curved walls are not available yet); Join at the ends and Automatic joining (greyed); Exterior on the left or Exterior on the right (the space bar swaps them) Door, Window Load Family; Model on site (greyed); Tag on Placement with Horizontal or Vertical, Leader and its length; Loaded tags… (greyed) Object Load Family; Model on site (greyed); Rotate after inserting: the object placed stays selected and Rotate starts Roof The shape: Gable, Hip or Flat; Slope, from 5° to 60°; Overhang, up to 2 m Stair Width, in millimetres; Railing Type, or None Dimensions What the cursor picks first on a wall: Wall centerlines or Wall faces Enlarged detail (callout) The scale of the new detail view, or Reference other view and the detail or free 2D view the callout points at (always on in a free 2D view) Area Outline Line or Pick lines; with Pick lines, Apply area rules or an Offset

The Ortho and Snap switches of the status bar work for every tool that draws lines: Ortho keeps the segments horizontal or vertical, Snap catches endpoints, midpoints and intersections. With Ortho off, holding Shift while drawing gives the same constraint; with it on, Shift releases it.

docs.title: Element panel
docs.text:
The element panel, on the right, shows and changes the parameters of what you are working on. Its header has the category and the name of what it shows, Close (which clears the selection) and More actions (⋯: Type Parameters and the actions of the contextual card). Under the header, its tabs:

The element panel: the properties of the view Tab What it holds Properties The type selector, then the parameters, in groups (Constraints, Graphics, Identification…). Click the name of a group to fold it. Values in grey are read-only: they are computed from the model. Apply, or Enter, confirms a value you are typing Materials For walls, floors and roofs: the layers of the type with their colours and thicknesses, and a preview of the layers Classification The category, the type and the IFC class Relations The level, the host, the doors and windows it hosts, the views and the schedules it appears in

The type selector shows the family in small letters, the type underneath, and a preview of the type: walls, floors and roofs as their layers, doors, windows and components as a small picture. Click it to choose another type: the selected elements change type, or, while a tool is active, the next element gets that type. Open it to search the types by name; they are grouped by family, each with its preview. The arrow keys move, Enter picks, Esc closes the list.

The type selector

What the panel shows depends on the situation:

Situation The panel shows Nothing selected, no tool The properties of the active view (scale, detail, graphic style…), or of the view clicked in the Project Index A tool active The type of the next element, as New Wall, New Door… One element selected Its type and its instance parameters Several elements of one category Their number, as Walls (3) Elements of different categories Multi-Select, Common (5), and how many of each category, as 3 × Walls

Lengths are written and read in the project's units (millimetres in a new project). You can type a value with its unit, for example 2.7m.

docs.title: Project Index
docs.text:
Views on the rail shows, under its tools, the Project Index: the views, schedules, sheets and families of the project in a tree. Click ⊟ or ⊞ to fold or unfold a branch.

The Project Index Branch What it contains Views (all) ▸ Floor Plans The floor plans of every level, from the lowest, and the callouts drawn in plans Views (all) ▸ Area Plans (…) The area plans, one branch per area scheme Views (all) ▸ Sections, Elevations The sections and the elevations Views (all) ▸ Detail Views The callouts drawn in sections Views (all) ▸ 3D Views {3D}, the default 3D view, and the saved 3D views Views (all) ▸ Free 2D Views The free 2D views Schedules/Quantities The project's schedules, then the predefined schedules Sheets (all) The sheets, as number - name Families The types of the project, by category: walls, doors, windows, floors, roofs, components and the others

The branches of area plans, sections, elevations, detail views and free 2D views appear only when they have something in them. The active view is written in bold.

With a view:

  • a click shows its properties in the element panel, without opening it;
  • a double-click opens it;
  • a right-click opens its menu: Open, Close (closes its windows), Duplicate View ▸ (Duplicate, Duplicate with Detailing), Apply view template…, Create view template from view…, Delete, Rename…, Properties.

The menu of a sheet has Apply view template to all views… instead of the two template items, and no Duplicate View. {3D} cannot be deleted or renamed.

With a schedule of the project, a click selects it, a double-click opens it, and the right-click menu has Open, Schedule Properties… and Delete. A predefined schedule opens with a click.

With a type, under Families, a double-click opens its type parameters; the right-click menu has Type Parameters, Duplicate…, Create Instance (starts the tool that places it, with that type) and Delete.

After a click in the Project Index, the keyboard moves in it: Up and Down go from row to row (the view's properties show in the element panel), Right opens a branch, Left closes it or goes up to the branch the row is in, Enter opens the view.

Views go on sheets from here too. Drag a plan, section, elevation, free 2D view, legend, saved 3D view or schedule onto the open sheet: its viewport follows the cursor and stays where you drop it. Or drop it on a sheet's name in the tree: the sheet opens and the viewport follows the cursor until you click. While you drag, the tree scrolls when the cursor nears its edge. The right-click menu of a sheet has Add View…. The views on a sheet are listed under it; the right-click menu of one has Remove from Sheet, and the menu of Sheets (all) has New Sheet…. In a 3D view the right-click menu also has Zoom to 3D Extents: the whole model, the elements hidden in the view too. A view already on a sheet is refused, with the reason on the command line; legends and schedules can go on several sheets. A saved 3D view is drawn on the sheet with the edges seen from its camera.

The right-click menu of a plan, section or free 2D view has Find Referring Views: the views that show its symbol and the sheets it is on; Go to View opens the one chosen.

docs.title: Views and families strip
docs.text:
The strip under the drawing area has three modes, chosen with the buttons on its left:

  • Views: live thumbnails of the views, grouped by All, Open (n), Plans, Sections, Elevations, 3D, Legends, Schedules and Sheets. The current view is framed, open views have an accent line. Click a thumbnail to open the view; right-click for the view's menu, with Open in the active window; drag it onto the open sheet, or onto a sheet's thumbnail, to place it there. + makes a new view: Default 3D View, Save View, Duplicate, Sheet or Schedule/Quantities.
  • Families: one preview for each type, grouped by family category. Click a preview to place that type; drag it into a plan to insert it where you let go. A door or a window dropped near a wall goes into it, along it.
  • Commands: the history of the command line. Click a line you typed to run it again.
The strip in Views mode

On the right, Show filters the thumbnails by discipline and phase, the search box by name, and three buttons set the size: Previews, Compact and Hide.

The strip in Families mode

docs.title: Panels
docs.text:
The element panel can move. Drag it by its header: it docks on the left or on the right of the drawing area, or floats where you let it go. The buttons at the top right of the panel dock it left, dock it right or make it float; Views ▸ Windows ▸ Panels shows or hides it and the other panels. Each panel stays where you put it in the next sessions.

While you drag a panel, only the places where it really docks are drawn, each as the panel it will become. The place under the pointer is drawn strongly, the others faintly. Elsewhere nothing is drawn, and the panel floats where you let it go.

docs.title: Dialogs
docs.text:
Every dialog opens in the middle of the screen, each time it opens, even if it was moved the last time or the window has changed size. Once open, it stays where it is: drag it by its title bar to move it. A change inside it, such as the Preview switch, does not move it.

Every dialog has a fixed size, which does not change with its content. The exception is the dialogs built around a long list or table (materials, visibility/graphics, object styles, filters, line styles and patterns, fill patterns, line weights, schedule properties, project and shared parameters, keyboard shortcuts, purge unused, IFC export classes, view templates): dragging one of their edges makes them larger, never smaller than they first open nor larger than the screen, and the list grows with them. They open again in the middle with the last size given.

docs.title: Drawing area and view windows
docs.text:
Every view you open is a window in the drawing area. A view opened again comes to the front; at least one window always stays open. At the top left of the view, the view selector shows its name: its menu lists the views and arranges the windows, and + beside it makes a new view. Views ▸ Windows arranges them too:

The view selector Tile What it does Switch View Lists the open windows; the active one is ticked Replicate Opens a second window on the active view, with its own zoom Cascade Overlapping windows, each with its title bar: drag a title to move a window, its edges to resize it Tile All the windows side by side, each with a title bar; the active one has a coloured title and frame Maximize The active window fills the drawing area; the others wait underneath Close others Closes every window except the active one Panels Shows or hides the Properties, the Project Index, the Command line, the Navigation bar, Keyboard Shortcuts and Recent Files

Click in a window to make it active: the tools work in the active window, the others only show the model. In Tile and Cascade, the × on a window's title bar closes it. Ctrl+Tab goes to the window you used before.

Tile puts the active window at the top left and the others after it, from the most recently active; Switch View lists them in the same order. Tile again after working in another window and that window comes first.

Options ▸ User Interface ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts lists the commands with their shortcuts. Search a command by name, or Filter the list (All, All Defined, All Not Defined, All Reserved); select a command, type the keys in Press new keys and click Assign. The same keys may go to several commands: typed in the drawing area, the status bar shows the first, the arrow keys go through the others and Enter or Space runs the one shown; Export… writes every shortcut to an XML file and Import… reads such a file back as your shortcuts (a file naming no command here is refused, and your shortcuts stay); Remove takes away the keys you added. Your shortcuts are kept for the next sessions and start the command when typed, as the built-in ones do.

A tool never changes the active view by itself. Started in a view where it cannot work (a roof or a room in a 3D view, a level in a plan, an area outside an area plan), it opens Go to View: the views that suit it, with the plan of the active level chosen first. Open View opens the chosen view and starts the tool there; Cancel leaves everything as it was. Edit Boundary of a floor, roof, stair or railing, from a section or an elevation, asks the same way for a plan of its level, and a new section or elevation leaves the plan you drew it in active. Move, Copy, a linear Repeat in Series and Mirror on Line also work in sections and elevations: along the view; the axis is the vertical plane at right angles to the view through its first point, however it is drawn. A radial Repeat in Series works in plans and 3D views: in a section or an elevation it stays chosen, but its clicks make nothing and the status bar asks for Linear.

docs.title: Views in separate windows
docs.text:
A view can leave the drawing area: Separate window in its menu (right-click it in the Project Index, on its thumbnail in the views strip, or on the title bar of a tiled window), or drag the title bar of a tiled or cascaded window out of the drawing area. On the computer the view opens in a system window of its own, which you can move to another monitor too, resize and maximise; on the web it floats in the page, because the browser opens no other windows. A view floating in the program also has System window, to move it into a system window.

You can separate several views at once. Each keeps its tools, its view bar and, in 3D, its orientation cube; the selection shows in all of them, and the active view is the last one you clicked. Back to the main window, at the top of the view, puts it back in the drawing area; a floating view also goes back when dragged onto the band at the top of the drawing area, which lights up. Closing the system window brings it back the same way. Where each separate view was stays with the project, and when it opens again the separate views come back to their places.

docs.title: Drawing in every view
docs.text:
A wall is drawn the same way in a plan and in a 3D view, on the level's plane: from the first click the wall being drawn follows the cursor, in the plan as its footprint and in 3D as its see-through solid, at its height and thickness; a dashed line carries its axis on, and others hold it in line with the points of the chain already clicked. The temporary dimension, blue with its witness lines and ticks, gives the length and the angle; type a length and press Enter to draw the wall that long. The snaps (endpoints, midpoints, intersections, perpendicular, other walls' faces and axes) work in 3D too. The wall selected in a 3D view shows, as in a plan, its temporary dimensions, the flip arrows and the ends to drag. In sections and elevations a wall is not drawn: Go to View offers a plan or the 3D view.

Roofs and floors are drawn in the 3D view too, on the plane of their level: Pick Walls takes the wall under the cursor (its top lights up in orange, Tab takes the whole chain), the lines are drawn with every sketch tool and with temporary dimensions, and Edit Footprint of a roof or a floor opens its sketch in 3D. Edit Boundary of a wall works in 3D on the wall's plane, and in a section or elevation that sees it face on.

While you draw or edit a sketch you can switch views (thumbnails, Project Index, separate windows): the tool stays active and goes on in the new view if it can work there. A chain of walls begun in a plan goes on in 3D from its last point, and a profile sketch begun in an elevation goes on in 3D. The wall being drawn and the sketch show in every open view at once.

docs.title: View bar
docs.text:
At the bottom centre of every view, a dark bar of buttons:

Button What it does Select and modify Ends the navigation mode, back to selecting, Esc Pan, Orbit (3D), Zoom With one on, the left button drags the view; Esc ends it Zoom to Fit Fits the whole view in the window, Home Zoom Options The zoom menu, see below The graphic style Wireframe, Lines, Shaded, Shaded with Edges, Flat Colors The detail Coarse, Medium or Fine Sun and shadows In 3D views, the sun and its shadows Crop Crop View crops the view to its crop region, or stops cropping; Show Crop Region shows or hides its frame Isolate Temporarily Hides or isolates elements or categories in this view until you reset it; framed while active Reveal Hidden Shows the hidden elements, to show them again Full screen The view alone in the window; Exit full screen comes back The view bar and the graphic styles

The scale of the view is on the right of the status bar, for example 1 : 100: it opens the list of scales; under Custom type another one, as 1 : 75, and press Enter. A sheet has no scale of its own: its views have theirs.

docs.title: Zoom
docs.text:
Zoom Options, on the view bar, opens the zoom menu: Zoom In, Zoom Out, Zoom in Region (drag a rectangle on the view; Esc gives up), Zoom Out (2x), Zoom to Fit, Zoom All to Fit (every open window), Zoom Sheet Size (the view at the size it prints), and Previous Pan/Zoom and Next Pan/Zoom, which go back and forth through the views of that window. Typed: ZR, ZO, ZF, ZA, ZS, ZP.

The navigation wheel is not available.

docs.title: Moving around in the views
docs.text:
In plans, sections, elevations and sheets Mouse wheel Zooms in and out at the cursor Drag with the middle button Pans Drag with the left button A selection window, or moves the selected elements (Selecting and modifying) Home Fits the whole view in the window In 3D views Drag with the right button, or Shift + middle button Orbits around the model Drag with the middle button Pans Drag with the left button A selection window, or moves the selected elements Mouse wheel Zooms in and out Home Fits the whole model in the window The BIMopen window with the sample house in the 3D view

A small tripod in the lower corner of the 3D view shows the directions of the axes: X red, Y green, Z blue. A saved 3D view remembers where you left it. On the selection, the move arrows let you drag it: drag an arrow to move along it, the centre to move freely in plan; the distance shows as you drag, and the release moves as Move does.

In 3D, the wheel zooms keeping the model point under the cursor in place, and the orbit turns about the centre of the selection, or about the point the view looks at when nothing is selected.

The Orientation cube, in the top corner of the 3D view, turns with the model. Its edges and corners are bevelled and every part is a target of its own: the six faces (TOP, BOTTOM, FRONT, BACK, RIGHT, LEFT, their names written on them in perspective and turning with them) look straight at that side; the twelve edge strips look from between two sides; the eight corner triangles from between three (an isometric view). The part under the pointer is tinted with the highlight colour, the one the view looks from now stays highlighted; a click turns the view there in a brief transition. Drag the cube to orbit.

The orientation cube

Under the cube the view's orientation is written: Front · perspective, Top – Front · perspective, Isometric · perspective, or Free · perspective when the view looks from no part of the cube.

When a face is seen straight on, four triangles round the cube (Turn up, Turn down, Turn left, Turn right) turn the view a quarter to the face beyond that side. The two curved arrows at the top right, Roll left and Roll right, turn the picture a quarter turn counterclockwise or clockwise.

The small house button at the bottom left, Starting view, goes back to the starting view; right-click it for Set as starting view, which makes the present view the starting one (each 3D view keeps its own, with the project). The small button at the bottom right, Cube menu, or a right-click on the cube, opens the menu: Orthographic / Perspective (for now the view is perspective only: Orthographic is greyed, «Not available yet»); Set as starting view; Zoom to Fit, which fits the model in the window; Options…, which opens the Orientation cube page of Options. Right to left (Arabic) the cube sits at the top left and the two small buttons change sides; the arrows stay where they point.

docs.title: The context menu of a view
docs.text:
Right-click in a view while no tool is active. If the cursor is on an element that is not selected, the element is selected first. The menu has, with a selection, the modify commands first (Move, Copy, Rotate, Align, Offset and the others), then:

  • Cancel: clears the selection;
  • Select All Instances ▸ Visible in View or ▸ In Entire Project: the elements of the same type; Select Previous: the selection made before;
  • Hide in view ▸ Elements or ▸ Category: hides the selected elements, or their whole categories, in this view;
  • Custom Graphics ▸ By category…: opens Visibility and Graphics on the categories of the selection;
  • Visibility and Graphics….

While a tool is active, a right-click opens the tool's menu instead, and the step in progress stays: Cancel (what Esc does, which still cancels the step), Repeat [command], Snap Overrides ▸ (the snap of the next point, as the two-letter keys do; in every view, see Snap), Zoom in Region, Zoom Out (2x), Zoom to Fit, Previous Pan/Zoom, Next Pan/Zoom and Properties. It is the same in plans, sections, elevations, 3D views and on sheets. With the menu open, Esc or a click in the view only closes it.

docs.title: Snap
docs.text:
Additional settings ▸ Snaps… (in the BIMopen style the Snaps… command) opens the Snap window, the same in both styles:

  • Snaps Off turns everything off (as the status bar's Snap switch, which stays as it was when the program opens again).
  • Length dimension snap increments and Angular dimension snap increments, each with its box: values separated by semicolons (by default 1000; 100; 10 mm and 90°; 45°; 15°; 5°; 1°). The zoom chooses the step: zoomed in, finer steps.
  • Object snaps: a box for Endpoint, Midpoint, Nearest, Work Plane Grid, Quadrant, Intersection, Center, Perpendicular, Tangent and Remote Objects, with their two letters; Check all and Check none. With Nearest off, the line under the cursor still offers its ends and its midpoint, even far away. Remote Objects (off at first) lines the point up, across or along, with the ends of lines far away, with a dashed guide.
  • Temporary overrides: the list of the two letters that hold for one point.
  • Restore Defaults puts everything back as it was at first.
Snap

The settings belong to the program, not to the project: they are kept between sessions.

While drawing from a point (walls, lines, grids, reference planes, sketches, and Rotate's second ray) the segment snaps its direction the same way in every view: horizontal or vertical, parallel or perpendicular to a line nearby, or a multiple of the angular increment the zoom gives; only when the cursor is a few pixels from that direction, otherwise the angle stays free. A dashed guide follows the direction, an arc with the value shows the angle, and the status bar says for instance Snap: Angle 30° · step 15°. The length is rounded to the length increment. Angle measured from, on the options bar, counts angles from the view's Horizontal axis or from the Previous segment. In the 3D view everything is measured on the work plane (the level's plane). At the command line snap {"angles":[45,15],"objects":{"quadrant":false}} changes the settings and snap alone shows them.

The anglesnap 0,0 3,0.02 command (also through MCP, and snap with two points) returns the direction a segment snaps to, by the same rules as every view.

At the top of the menu, Repeat [command] starts the last tool you used again; Enter does the same when no tool is active and the command line is empty. The menu is the same in plans, sections and 3D views.

docs.title: Command search and command line
docs.text:
The command search: commands, elements and views that match what is typed

Press Ctrl+K, or click the search box in the middle of the top bar, and type a few letters: the list shows the commands, views, sheets, schedules, elements and materials that match. Click a result, or choose it with the arrow keys and press Enter: a command starts, a view opens, an element is selected and shown, a material opens in Materials. The search finds every command of the tool panel, the contextual card's too (with a view selected on a sheet, «activate» finds Activate View), and runs it as its tile does.

The search box is also the command line. You do not need to click it: whatever you type in a view while no field is being edited goes there. Enter runs a keyboard shortcut (WA, DR, ZF…) or a command with its arguments (wall 0,0 5,0) as typed; Up and Down bring back the lines typed before. The log of what has been done, the commands run, their results and the errors in red, is in Command log at the right end of the status bar and in the Commands mode of the strip. The command line chapter describes the commands.

docs.title: Status bar
docs.text:
On the left, the status bar shows the project, the version and the active view, then:

The status bar
  • while a tool is active, what the tool expects, for example WALL next point [Esc to finish]:;
  • with no tool, the category and the type of the element under the cursor, as Walls : Exterior wall - Clay block 300 + ETICS;
  • while you drag, the length of the move, as Move: 1500;
  • otherwise the last line of the command log.

On the right: the coordinates of the cursor (X, Y, Z) in metres; the active level, whose menu opens the plan of another level; the number of selected elements, which opens Filter; the switches Select and Drag (drag elements without selecting them first), Snap, Grid and Ortho; the scale of the view; and Command log.

docs.title: Selecting, in short
docs.text:
The selecting and modifying chapter describes selection in full. The essentials:

  • click an element to select it; click an empty point to clear the selection;
  • Ctrl + click adds an element to the selection, Shift + click takes it out; Tab highlights the next element under the cursor, or a chain of joined walls;
  • drag from left to right to select what is entirely inside the rectangle, from right to left to select what it touches;
  • drag a selected element to move it;
  • Ctrl+A selects the elements of the open plan's level, or of the whole model in a 3D view; Del deletes the selection; Esc clears it.

On a touch screen the same is done with the fingers and the pen: see touch mode.

docs.title: Keyboard shortcuts
docs.text:
BIMopen has two kinds of shortcuts: keys, such as Ctrl+Z, which act at once, and typed shortcuts, such as WA, which you type letter by letter. At the command line a typed shortcut waits for Enter, like any command; typed over the drawing area, it acts as soon as it is complete when nothing longer begins with its letters (see below). Typed shortcuts are the same in every language.

On macOS, Cmd takes the place of Ctrl.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
Key What it does Ctrl+Z Undoes the last change Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z Redoes the change just undone Ctrl+S Saves the project; a project never saved asks for a file name Ctrl+P Opens Print Ctrl+A Selects the elements of the open plan's level, or of the whole model in a 3D view Del Deletes the selected elements, and the elements they host Home Fits the whole view in its window F1 Opens the page of this manual about the open dialog, the tile under the mouse or the active tool Esc Cancels the step in progress; pressed again, ends the tool; with no tool, clears the selection Enter Runs the line typed at the command line; confirms a value in the element panel Up / Down At the command line, the lines typed before Space While drawing walls, swaps the exterior and interior side; while placing a component or a detail component, rotates it Shift While drawing, keeps segments horizontal or vertical (or frees them, when Ortho is on); with a click or a window, takes elements out of the selection; while dragging, frees a joined wall or keeps the move horizontal or vertical Ctrl + click Adds an element to the selection; held when a drag starts, places a copy Tab / Shift+Tab Highlights the next (previous) element under the cursor, or a chain of joined walls and lines Ctrl+Left Selects again what was selected before Left Right Up Down Move the selection a small step; with Shift, ten steps

Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y, Ctrl+A, Del and Home act on the model only while you are not typing in a field: in a field they act on the text.

In a floor, roof, stair or railing sketch, Esc (or a double-click) also finishes the sketch when it has enough points.

In the Text Note dialog, Ctrl+Enter inserts the note and Esc cancels it.

Alt pressed and released, or F10, shows the key tips of the rail and the tool panel. With no tool active and nothing typed, Enter repeats the last tool. After a click in the Project Index, the arrow keys and Enter move in its tree.

docs.title: Mouse
docs.text: In plans and sections In 3D views Wheel Zoom at the cursor Zoom Middle button, drag Pan Pan; with Shift, orbit Left button, drag Selection window (left to right: inside; right to left: touching), or moves the selected elements The same Right button Context menu; with a tool active, the tool's menu (Cancel, Snap Overrides ▸…) The same; dragging, orbit Double-click Finishes a sketch –

docs.title: Typed shortcuts
docs.text:
Type the letters while no field is being edited, then press Enter. Without arguments, a shortcut starts the tool or opens the dialog; with arguments, it runs the command at once (see Command line and MCP).

With the cursor in the drawing area, the letters go to the command line (in the BIMopen style, to the search), and a shortcut acts as soon as it is typed, with no Enter, when no longer shortcut or command name begins with its letters: VR (cut heights), WT (tile), ZE, ZF, ZA, ZP, ZR, ZO, ZS, HR, HH, HC, IC, DL (detail line), RT (room label), TG (tag by category), TX, CC (copy), MV, RM, LL (level), RC (revision cloud), PP (shows or hides Properties), PT, RP, and the shortcuts you added. The others begin longer names and wait for the next letter, a space (arguments follow) or Enter: VG (vgsub…), HI (hide), DI (dim), AL (align), WA (wall), DR (draworder), UN (undo), MA (mask); so dim, wall 0,0 5,0 or WA 0,0 5,0 typed over the view run as typed. MA and PT say in the status bar that they are not available yet; RP starts the reference plane. Typed in the command line itself, a line waits for Enter.

While a tool waits for a point, in every view (plans, free 2D views, sections, elevations, the 3D view on its work plane, sketches), two letters override the snaps for that point only: SE (endpoint), SM (midpoint), SN (nearest), SW (work plane grid), SQ (quadrant), SI (intersection), SC (center), SP (perpendicular), ST (tangent), SR (remote objects), SZ (close), SO (no snap); SS ends the override in force. They are also chosen in the right button's Snap Overrides ▸; those a longer name begins with need Enter. The status bar says so, and Esc or the point taken ends it. With several snaps under the cursor, Tab goes to the next and Shift+Tab to the previous. Shortcuts added in Keyboard Shortcuts under a snap's name work as its two letters.

docs.title: Modelling
docs.text: Shortcut Command Starts WA or W wall Wall DR door Door WN window Window SB floor Floor (the Flooring button) RF roof Roof CM component Object ST stair Stairs RA railing Railing CG curtaingrid Curtain grid MU mullion Mullion CP curtainpanel Curtain wall panel GR grid Grid RM room Room RS roomsep Room separator PA areaplan The Area Plan dialog CA areaboundary Area outline – area Area LG legend Color fill legend SC colorscheme The Color Schemes dialog

docs.title: Modifying
docs.text: Shortcut Command Starts MV or M move Move CO copy Copy RO rotate Rotate MM mirror Mirror on Axis DM mirror Mirror on Line AR array Repeat in Series OF offset Offset AL align Align TR trim Shorten/Lengthen SL split Split Element SG split Split with Joint RE resize Scale PN pin Fix: pins the selection UP unpin Unpins the selection SA selectinstances Selects all instances of the selection's types visible in the view DEL delete Deletes the selection U undo Undoes the last change

docs.title: Annotating and detailing
docs.text:
Shortcut Command Starts DI dim Aligned dimension DL lineardim Linear dimension DA angulardim Angular dimension TX text Text TG tag Tags the untagged doors and windows of the level – detailline Detail line RG region Filled region – mask Masking region CD detailcomponent Detail component RD repeatingdetail Repeating detail IS insulation Insulation

Note

Typed alone, DL starts the detail line; followed by points at the command line, it draws a linear dimension (lineardim).

docs.title: Views and settings
docs.text:
Shortcut Command Starts or opens SE section Section EL elevation Elevation DT callout Callout (the Detail button) DS splitsegment Split Segment of a section VD draftingview The Free 2D View dialog PP floorplan The Floor Plan dialog DV duplicateview Duplicates the active view VG or VV vg Visibility and Graphics WF, HL, SD – Wireframe, Lines, Shaded: the graphic style of the active view HH, HI – Hide Element, Isolate Element for now HC, IC – Hide Category, Isolate Category for now HR – Reset Isolate Temporarily EH, VH – Hide in view: the selected elements, their category RH – Reveal Hidden, on and off TL thinlines Thin lines, on and off SO objectstyle Styles by Category MA material Materials UN units Project units PU purge Purge unused – filter Filters – viewtemplate View templates – applytemplate Apply a view template to the active view – linestyle Line styles – fillpattern Fill patterns – saveview3d Saves the {3D} view with a name – renameview Renames the active view

The commands with – have no short form, but their whole name works the same way. help lists every command and its short forms.

The zoom commands have typed shortcuts too: ZR zoom in region, ZO zoom out (2x), ZF zoom to fit, ZA zoom all to fit, ZS zoom sheet size, ZP previous pan/zoom. Views ▸ Windows ▸ Panels ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts gives any command shortcuts of your own (The interface).

docs.title: Projects and files
docs.text:
This chapter describes how a project is created, opened, saved and exchanged with other programs, its settings and the options of BIMopen itself.

The application menu, on BIMopen's mark

docs.title: Creating a project
docs.text:
application menu ➤ New ➤ Project… opens New project:

  • Template file: BIMopen's default template, or the one set in Options ➤ File Locations; a template file chosen with Browse…; or None, which starts from two levels and one type of each kind.
  • Create new: Project or Project Template.
New project

A project made from a template has everything the template had: types, settings, views, sheets, project information and print settings. Saving it asks for a name, so the template is not overwritten.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text: A template is a .bimtpl file. application menu ➤ Save As ➤ Template… saves the open project as a template; a project created as a Project Template, or a template opened, is saved as a template too.

docs.title: Opening a project
docs.text:
Ctrl+O or application menu ➤ Open… opens a project. application menu ➤ Recent Documents lists the latest projects, the most recent first; a pin keeps a project in the list. Without a file, BIMopen starts on Recent Files, with the recent projects, Open…, New and the Sample project (unless Enable Recent Files page at startup is unticked in the options). Dropping a project file on the window opens it too.

A project already open in another BIMopen window opens read-only: Save asks for a new name. If BIMopen stopped without saving (a crash, a power cut), opening the project again brings the unsaved work back as unsaved changes.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text:
Ctrl+S, or a click on the save state in the top bar, saves the project; until then the file stays as it was last saved, and the top bar says Unsaved changes. application menu ➤ Save As ➤ Project… writes it to a new file and goes on there.

Save As ➤ Options… opens File Save Options: Maximum backups keeps that many earlier versions beside the file (house.0001.bimopen, house.0002.bimopen…), deleting the oldest; Compact file rewrites the file without its obsolete parts at the next save.

When a changed project stays unsaved for the interval set in Options ➤ General (Save reminder interval, 30 minutes to start with), Save Reminder offers to save it, not to save it, or to change the interval.

One project is open at a time: the project opened takes the place of the one open, and the views of that one close with it. Opening the project already open leaves it as it is, when it has no unsaved changes; with changes, answering No to the question to save them drops them and opens the file again as last saved, as closing it without saving and reopening it.

Before New, Open…, a recent document, a dropped file, open at the command line, the sample project, or closing the window, a changed project asks Save changes to …?: Yes saves it, No drops the changes, Cancel keeps it open.

In the browser, Open… uses the browser's file chooser, and Save downloads the file; backups, crash recovery and read-only opening need a file on disk and are desktop-only.

docs.title: Project information
docs.text: Settings ➤ Settings ➤ Project information sets the project's name, number, client, address, issue date and status: the title blocks of every sheet show them.

docs.title: Project units
docs.text:
Settings ➤ Settings ➤ Project units lists the quantities (length, area, volume, angle, slope and the others) with a sample of each, and the Decimal symbol/digit grouping. Format… of a quantity sets its unit, its Rounding (a number of decimals, or Custom with an Increment factor, such as 5 mm), its Unit symbol, Suppress trailing zeros, the plus sign for positive values and digit grouping.

Project units, then Format… of a quantity

docs.title: Sun Settings
docs.text: Settings ➤ Additional settings ➤ Sun Settings opens the sun settings of the active view, the same as the sun button of the view control bar (see Views and graphics).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
application menu ➤ Options has four tabs; the choices are kept between sessions.

Tab What it sets General The save reminder interval User Interface The theme (Light or Dark), the language, the interface style and size; Enable Recent Files page at startup; in the Classic style, the ribbon tab after a selection ends or a tool closes (Stay on the Modify tab or Return to the previous tab) and Display the contextual tab on selection; Tooltip Assistance (None, Minimal, Normal, Extra High) Graphics Invert background color, Selection color, Highlight color, Use anti-aliasing for 3D views, Temporary Dimension Text Appearance (size and background) File Locations Default template file path (the template of New) and Default path for user files (where the file dialogs open) Options, User Interface tab

docs.title: Copying settings from a project
docs.text:
Settings ➤ Settings ➤ Copy Settings from Project copies settings from another project into this one. In Select Items To Copy, choose the project with Browse… (Copy from:), then tick what to copy: the types of walls, floors, roofs, doors and windows, stairs, railings, curtain panels and mullions, line styles, filled region types, materials, fill and line patterns, line weights, styles by category, view templates, filters, viewport types, title blocks, the project units, the print settings and the project information (Check all, None).

Copying settings from another project

What is copied brings along what it uses: a wall type its materials, a material its patterns, a view template its filters. When names are already in the project, Duplicate Types asks whether to Overwrite them or to transfer the New Only. The whole transfer is one step of undo.

docs.title: Exporting to IFC
docs.text:
application menu ➤ Export ➤ IFC… writes the model in IFC4: walls with their axis and body, openings, doors, windows, floors, roofs, stairs, railings, curtain walls, furniture and rooms as spaces, on their storeys.

Export ➤ Options ➤ IFC Options… opens IFC Export Classes: the IFC class of each category; Not Exported leaves a category out, and Default goes back to the standard classes. The classes are kept with the project.

docs.title: Opening IFC files
docs.text:
application menu ➤ Open ➤ IFC… makes a new project from an IFC2x3 or IFC4 file, in metres or millimetres: storeys become levels, walls are rebuilt from their axis (or from the long side of their body), slabs become floors, doors and windows go in the walls their openings cut, and spaces become rooms. The messages count what was not read.

Open ➤ IFC Options… opens Import IFC Options: what each IFC class becomes (walls, floors, doors, windows, rooms or Not Imported), and Default. The choices are kept between sessions.

docs.title: .rvt files
docs.text: Opening a .rvt file is experimental: today it reads only the project name and the level names, so the new project has its levels and no walls, doors, windows or floors. The messages say so after the import. To exchange models with other BIM software, use IFC4.

docs.title: Other exports
docs.text: Printing to PDF and exporting images are described in Sheets, schedules and printing; schedules export as delimited text from the same chapter. bimopen-cli convert exports from the command line (see Command line and MCP).

docs.title: Selecting and modifying
docs.text: Before most changes you select what to change. This chapter describes how elements are highlighted and selected, how a selection is refined, how selected elements are dragged, and the tools of the Modify group. Everything here works the same in the desktop app and in the browser.

docs.title: Highlighting and selecting
docs.text:
A wall selected in the plan: its contextual card on the left, its properties in the element panel on the right

Move the cursor over an element: its lines are drawn wider, the status bar at the bottom of the window names it (category and type, as Walls : Exterior wall…), and after a moment the same words appear under the cursor. Click to select the highlighted element. A selected element is drawn in the selection colour in every view where it shows, and the count at the right end of the status bar says how many elements are selected.

A right click on an element selects it and opens the context menu. Esc, or a click on an empty spot, clears the selection.

To… Do this add an element to the selection Ctrl + click take an element out of the selection Shift + click select what is wholly inside a window drag from left to right select what a window touches drag from right to left (the window is dashed) add, or take away, what a window catches drag with Ctrl, or with Shift select again what was selected before Ctrl+Left, or right click ▸ Select Previous A window from right to left selects what it touches

Windows work in plans, sections, sheets and 3D views. In a 3D view the left button selects; the right button orbits and the middle button pans (see The interface).

docs.title: Elements close together: TAB
docs.text: When elements lie close together or one over the other, the one highlighted may not be the one you want. Keep the cursor still and press Tab: the next element under the cursor is highlighted and the status bar names it. Shift+Tab goes back. Click to select the highlighted element. In a 3D view Tab goes from the nearest element to the ones behind it; on a sheet, through views placed one over the other.

docs.title: Chains of walls and lines
docs.text:
Walls and lines joined end to end form a chain. With the cursor on one of them, Tab highlights the whole chain (the status bar says Chain of n joined elements); a click selects it. A chain can mix walls with room separators and area outlines; detail lines chain with the detail lines of their view. Where three or more meet, the chain goes on along the one that makes the smallest angle with the last; a wall that stops against another one between its ends takes the chain on along that wall.

TAB: the whole chain of walls

Part of a chain. Select the first element of the part, move the cursor over the last one and press Tab: the elements between them are highlighted. Tab again highlights the whole chain, a third time the last element alone. Click to select what is highlighted. On a closed chain the part goes round by the side where the cursor is: near the end of the last element that one way round reaches first.

Elements joined at a point. Select an element and keep the cursor on it, near an end where others are joined. Tab highlights it with the nearest one joined there; Tab again, every element joined there. Click to select them.

A selected chain. Where two selected walls or lines meet, a round control appears. Drag it to move the joint: the selected ends there move together and stay joined; elements not selected are left where they are. Drag the chain with Shift to move it whole, horizontally or vertically; drag it with Ctrl to place a copy.

docs.title: Filtering a selection
docs.text:
Click the count in the status bar, or Filter on the contextual card, to open Filter. It lists the categories in the selection, how many elements each has, and the total. Untick a category to leave its elements out: the selection and the count in the status bar follow at once. Check all and Check none tick or untick every category. OK keeps the selection, Cancel brings back the one you started with.

Filter

docs.title: Select All Instances
docs.text: Right-click an element ▸ Select All Instances, then Visible in View (the elements of the same type shown in the active view) or In Entire Project. Typing SA and Enter does the same as Visible in View. The element must have a type: rooms, for example, have none.

docs.title: Dragging elements
docs.text:
Drag a selected element to move it; the whole selection moves together, and one drag is undone by one Ctrl+Z. A temporary dimension shows the move, and the status bar its length (Move: 1500). With Select and Drag turned on in the status bar, an element can be dragged without selecting it first; with it off, a drag that starts on an element not selected draws a window.

  • A wall joined at its ends to walls that are not selected moves square to itself only, and the joined walls stretch to stay joined. Walls that stop against it follow too. Hold Shift to move it freely; the joined walls still follow.
  • Any other element moves freely; hold Shift to keep the move horizontal or vertical.
  • Doors and windows move with their wall and keep their place along it. Dragged on their own, they slide along the wall; dropped on another wall, they move into it.
  • Hold Ctrl when you start dragging to place a copy instead.

Elements are dragged in plans, sections and elevations (along the view), on sheets (views), and in 3D views, where they move on the horizontal plane where you grabbed them. The arrow keys move the selection a small step, rounded to a tidy value at the zoom of the view; with Shift, ten steps.

docs.title: The Modify tools
docs.text:
The Modify group of the contextual card has three rows: Align, Offset, Mirror on Axis, Mirror on Line, Split Element, Split with Joint; Move, Copy, Rotate, Shorten/Lengthen, Shorten/Lengthen one element, Shorten/Lengthen several elements; Repeat in Series, Scale, Fix, Unpin, Delete. The status bar says what each tool expects next, and the options strip shows its options. Esc cancels the step in progress; pressed again, it ends the tool.

Move, Copy, Rotate, the two Mirror tools, Repeat in Series and Scale work on the selection. Started with nothing selected, they let you select first (clicks, Ctrl, windows, Tab), then go on when you press Enter or End on the options strip.

Move, Copy and Rotate also work in 3D views: their points are taken on the plane of the level clicked.

Before each click the tool shows what the click would do: the selection drawn where it would go (moved, copied, turned, mirrored about the axis under the cursor, offset to the cursor's side, aligned to the reference), following the cursor, with the distance or the angle beside it.

Where a tool asks for a second point, you can type a distance (or an angle) instead and press Enter: it shows next to the cursor while you type, and is measured towards the cursor.

docs.title: Move
docs.text:
Click a base point, then the destination. The tool ends and the elements stay selected. Options:

Move: the preview, then the result
  • Constrain: the move is along or square to the selected wall (horizontal or vertical for other elements);
  • Disjoin: walls joined to the moved ones do not follow, and a door or window can be moved onto another wall;
  • Copy: copies are placed instead; with Multiple, one at each click until Esc.

docs.title: Copy
docs.text: As Move, but a copy is placed. With Multiple, a copy at each click until Esc; Constrain as for Move.

docs.title: Rotate
docs.text:
The centre of rotation shows at the middle of the selection; drag it to put it elsewhere. Click the first ray, then the second: the selection turns by the angle between them, shown by a temporary angular dimension. Instead of the second ray, type the angle and press Enter, or type it in Angle on the options strip and press Enter. Copy turns a copy; without Disjoin, walls joined to the turned ones follow.

Rotate: the angle before the second click

docs.title: Mirror
docs.text: Mirror on Axis: click a wall, a grid or a line as the axis. Mirror on Line: click two points. Copy is ticked: a mirrored copy is placed; untick it to mirror the elements themselves.

docs.title: Repeat in Series
docs.text:
Linear: click two points. Number is how many elements in all. With Move To: 2° the two points give the spacing; with Last, the last element goes to the second point and the others are spread evenly. Constrain keeps the direction along or square to the selection.

Radial: drag the centre where the copies turn about, click the first ray, then the second (or type the angle and press Enter, also in Angle). With 2° the angle is between neighbours, with Last it is the whole span.

docs.title: Offset
docs.text:
Moves a wall or a line square to itself, or places a copy (Copy is ticked).

  • Numerical: set Offset, then click the element on the side it should go to. Press Tab first to offset the whole chain (of the same category) as one: its corners are kept.
  • Graphical: click the element (Tab for the chain), then two points: the distance between them, square to the element, is the offset. You can type it instead. Ctrl copies.

docs.title: Align
docs.text: Click the reference, then the element to align: the face of the element nearest to your click goes onto the face of the reference nearest to its click. Prefer chooses Wall faces or Wall centerlines. After aligning, a padlock shows on the aligned face: click it to keep the two aligned, so that moving the reference moves the other one too. Without Multiple Alignment the next click picks a new reference; with it (or holding Ctrl) you can align several elements to the same one. Esc once starts a new alignment, twice ends the tool.

docs.title: Shorten/Lengthen
docs.text:
Walls and lines are trimmed or extended; click each one on the part to keep.

  • Shorten/Lengthen: two elements, which then meet at a corner;
  • Shorten/Lengthen one element: the boundary, then the element;
  • Shorten/Lengthen several elements: the boundary, then each element in turn.

docs.title: Split Element and Split with Joint
docs.text: Split Element: click a wall or a line where it should become two. With Delete Inner Segment, click two points: the part between them is removed, with the doors and windows in it. Split with Joint: set Joint Gap, then click: the two parts are that far apart.

docs.title: Scale
docs.text: Walls and lines (and the position of dimensions) can be scaled; with anything else selected, Scale is not available. Graphical: click the origin, the end of a first vector, the end of a second one: the elements are scaled by the ratio of the two lengths (you can type the second one). Numerical: set Scale Factor, then click the origin. Doors and windows keep their distance from the middle of their wall.

docs.title: Fix and Unpin
docs.text: Fix keeps the selected elements where they are: they cannot be dragged, moved by a tool or deleted, and a message says so. A pinned element shows a pushpin when selected; click the pushpin, or use Unpin, to free it.

docs.title: Delete, undo and redo
docs.text: Delete (or the Del key) removes the selection and what it hosts; pinned elements stay. Ctrl+Z undoes the last change and Ctrl+Y redoes it: each tool, drag or nudge is one step.

docs.title: Typed shortcuts
docs.text: Type the letters and press Enter: MV Move, CO Copy, RO Rotate, MM Mirror on Axis, DM Mirror on Line, AR Repeat in Series, OF Offset, AL Align, TR Shorten/Lengthen, SL Split Element, SG Split with Joint, RE Scale. PN pins and UP unpins the selection, SA selects all its instances visible in the view. Keyboard shortcuts lists them all.

docs.title: Not yet available
docs.text:
• Tab to reach a part of an element: a curtain panel or mullion, a part of a stacked wall;
  • Select All Instances from a type in the Project Index;
  • Group and Associate of Repeat in Series;
  • splitting walls along a horizontal line in elevations and 3D views;
  • cut, copy and paste through the clipboard, Paste Aligned, Create Same.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: This chapter collects situations that can surprise you, and what to do about them. It grows with the manual: each area of the realignment adds its own.

docs.title: The web app shows «BIMopen non si è avviato» and an error
docs.text:
The browser could not give BIMopen a graphics surface: the message ends with webgl2 not available or with a WebGPU error. BIMopen in the browser needs WebGPU or WebGL2.

  • Turn on hardware acceleration in the settings of the browser, then reload the page.
  • Try another browser, or a newer version of the same one.
  • Add ?webgl to the address to use WebGL2 even where WebGPU exists but does not work.

docs.title: The desktop app does not build on Linux
docs.text:
The interface needs the development files of xkbcommon, Wayland and GTK 3. On Debian and Ubuntu:

sudo apt-get install -y libxkbcommon-dev libwayland-dev libgtk-3-dev

docs.title: The element panel or the Project Index has disappeared
docs.text: Views ▸ Windows ▸ Panels shows or hides them: tick them again there. The Properties tile of the contextual card also shows the element panel again. A click on the rail entry already chosen folds the tool panel: click it again to open it.

docs.title: What I type ends up at the command line
docs.text: Whatever you type while no field is being edited goes to the command line, the search box of the top bar: this is how typed shortcuts work. To type in a field of the element panel or of a dialog, click the field first.

docs.title: A tile is greyed
docs.text: Some tools work only in the right view, and their tip says why. Area Outline and Area need an open area plan: the tip says Open an area plan first. Save View needs an open 3D view; Document ▸ Sheets ▸ View needs an open sheet; Undo and Redo are greyed when there is nothing to undo or redo.

docs.title: DL starts a dimension instead of a detail line
docs.text: DL is the short form of the linear dimension. To draw detail lines, use Document ▸ Detail ▸ Detail line, or type detailline.

docs.title: «no wall at that point»
docs.text: A door or a window must be placed in a wall. Click on the wall itself, or give a point on its line at the command line.

docs.title: A height set at the command line is enormous
